compute.note: Parameters: 64 from the method string (high confidence); the circuit code builds 64 one-parameter gates (SU2_symmetrized._get_dimerizarion_layers: range(1) x 4 shifts x (8 + 8) pairs), which reproduces it. Iterations: 2000 = 1000 natural-gradient steps without symmetry projection, then 1000 continuing with the 64-element projector (n_iter default 1000; main.py is called twice and passes only lr). As published, Optimizer.optimize() ends with "return res.x" on the circuit object, which has no attribute x, so the first call exits with an AttributeError and "&&" would skip the symmetric run; the step counts are therefore what the code intends, not what it can be shown to have run, hence confidence low. Samples: none; the method string says exact gradients on a state vector. The code has no exact branch that main.py reaches: it draws binomial estimates with the default 2^36 shots (--log2samples default 36), which is exact to about 4e-6 relative. The script passes --j2=0.0 with --lattice=triangle4x4, and hamiltonians.HeisenbergTriangle adds the diagonal (third-direction) bonds only "if not np.isclose(j2, 0.0)": as published it simulates the 4x4 square-lattice Heisenberg model (exact -44.914), not the triangular one the row's energy -34.1780764 belongs to (exact -34.222). The step count and circuit are still the code's; the Hamiltonian is not the row's. Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 26f221f (2022-10-18, Nikita Astrakhantsev); the program was added to methods in 6887677 (2024-08-10) ("wip: added the VQE simulator"; next commit "VQE simulator: dusted-off version runs"), so it is a later reconstruction. The VarBench SM (arXiv:2302.04919 Sec. S3 D) describes the ansatz and the natural-gradient update but no step count. No device or time is recorded. || pass 2026-09-27: circuit_schedule restored from route 1b's pass (merge.mjs copied only the BLOCK fields and dropped it), plus dimension = C(16, 8) = 12870: the S^z = 0 sector without lattice symmetry the state vector lives in (the calibration runs measured the step time at exactly this D). runs keep the intended 1000 + 1000 steps; as published the first call ends in the res.x AttributeError and && skips the symmetric run, so 1000 steps actually execute (verify/agent-A.md item 6, DOUBTFUL x2; no change).

The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 16*15/2 = 120 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 16 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nk.VMC with nk.optimizer.SR(QGTOnTheFly) (n_parameters < n_samples). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.0027 vs sqrt(stored variance 7.37471 / 2^20) = 0.0027: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in ad306c2 (2022-10-19, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs). || pass 2026-09-27: evaluation from the script's code path. proposals_per_sample = N x (s + d)/s = 16 x (1 + 0)/1 = 16: batch 1024 = n_samples = n_chains (one sample per chain per step), n_discard_per_chain = 0, sweep_size = hilbert.size = N (NetKet default, every proposal a full forward). sr: n_parameters = 120 < n_samples = 1024, so nk.VMC with SR(QGTOnTheFly(), solver=solve); solve() calls A.to_dense(), which applies the lazy S to the P = 120 unit vectors (P jvp + transpose mat-vecs over all 1024 samples per step): kind onthefly_dense (verify/agent-A.md item 1: 3.9-23x the network count for the 26 rows with P < 1024). complex false: --dtype default float32, param_dtype=args.dtype, no script overrides it. local_energy all: NetKet's get_conn_padded; the NetKet LocalOperator pads to the batch maximum of nonzero elements, so on Heisenberg/J1-J2 'all' overstates the local energy by about 10-30 % (verify/agent-A.md item 4). Caveat: the scripts (2024-07-30, commit bba4595 the same day replaced cg(maxiter=20) by solve and added VMC_SRt) postdate the 2022 energies; the SR path of the original runs is not known (agent-A.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md). || pass 2026-09-29: evaluation.jacobian "real" (high confidence), the matrix the code's SR builds (DATA.md).

verified.note: scripts/Heisenberg/triangular_16_P/vmc_jastrow.sh: 'python3 vmc.py --ham heis_tri --boundary peri --sign mars --ham_dim 2 --L 4 --zero_mag --net jas --seed 123 --show_progress' -> 4x4 triangular lattice (ColoredJ1J2 back_diag=False: square grid + (i,j)-(i+1,j+1) diagonals), periodic; NetKet Heisenberg J = 1 in Pauli form with Marshall rotation on the square bonds only (sign_rule=[True, False], a unitary: the diagonals join same-sublattice sites); Sz = 0 (total_sz=0, MetropolisExchange); real float32 Jastrow (nk.models.Jastrow); 10^4 SR steps; final estimate over 2^20 samples (vmc.py lines 268-269). sigma/sqrt(Var/2^20) = 1.018: the stored sigma is the error of that final estimate. 1.1276 above the exact -34.22205967006502. M2/M6 flags (if any): real float32 parameters make the amplitudes positive, so on this frustrated lattice the ansatz cannot carry the ground-state signs; no constant shift is involved and the energy is a valid bound. History: entered ad306c2 (2022-10-19, Dian Wu) as -33.0945 | 0.0027 | 7.37471 | Jastrow baseline; linked fdb4bfb (2024-07-30). Program files postdate the value (scripts added to varbench/methods 2024-07-30); they document the settings after the run.
